issues.description: The problem statement UML declares StockIngredient.price as an int and specifies a constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), and the provided solution uses an int price, but the template StockIngredient implementation uses a double price and a constructor taking (String, double, int). This type mismatch (double vs int) across artifacts will cause compilation problems when students implement SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice (which returns int and sums ingredient prices) and creates confusion about the correct type to use for price.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the price type consistent across all artifacts. Prefer updating the template to use int for the price field and constructor parameter (and change getPrice() to return int) to match the UML in the problem statement and the solution. Alternatively, if floating-point prices are intended, update the UML and the solution to use double consistently.
